Subject: Post-call: retrieval fit + reranker recommendations for Cygnus Health

Sarah — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery on RAG behavior for the provider knowledge base: 

- Goal we heard: high precision for citations in clinical answers, <10% hallucination rate on our eval set, 95% citation coverage for eligibility-policy queries.
- Primary constraints: 300ms per-turn latency SLO for UI flows, live updates to docs every 24 hours, and retention/PII scrubbed at ingestion.

What we'll deliver next (proposed):
1) A short benchmark packet with two model configurations + retrieval profiles (attached: cygnus-rag-benchmarks-20270322.pdf).
2) Prompt set v1 for your clinical / eligibility prompts (attached).
3) Reranker A/B: cross-encoder (high-precision) vs hybrid recall-boosted bi-encoder+light re-rank (faster) — we'll run on your sample and include recall@10 / grounding-precision numbers.

Immediate asks from your side: please share the 10–15 canonical queries we discussed (preferably labeled by priority) and a small sandbox snapshot (CSV/MD with doc ids) or a secure drive link.

Proposed short timeline:
- Tue/Wed: we run initial retrieval profile (chunking, embedding model, store) on your snapshot.
- End of week: deliver benchmark PDF + a reranker comparison table.
- Next week: quick sync to review results and pick the candidate production profile.

I've attached the prompt set and the preliminary benchmark artifacts. If this aligns, we'll schedule a 30-min technical review with Dev and Monica.

Best,
Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Sarah. Short answers to your clarifications and an initial recommendation: 

- Embeddings: we'll start with redwood-embed-3 for chunk-level vectors (your content is clinical and benefits from higher semantic fidelity). If need be we'll compare to open alternatives (e.g., text-embedding-3-small) in the benchmark.

- Hallucination measurement: we report a combined metric — grounding-precision (precision@k on cited passages), and a manual sample review rate for semantic hallucinations on 200 prompts (binary yes/no per sample). For the benchmark packet we'll include: grounding-precision@1/3/5, citation-coverage, and a per-prompt hallucination flag frequency.

- Reranker recommendation: given your priority for citation accuracy, start with a cross-encoder reranker (we used a distilled cross-encoder in the attached CSV). We'll run a latency sensitivity sweep: cross-encoder (best precision), hybrid (bi-encoder recall + lightweight cross-encoder re-rank top 30), and an aggressive quantized cross-encoder for lower cost.

Technical sync suggestion: Wed 24 Mar 10:00 PT — Dev will share the retrieval config we plan to test (chunk size, overlap, embed model, vector store). If that works I can send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Ben

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Technical notes: retrieval config we'll test (attached CSV)

Hi all — attaching the reranker-comparison-table.csv and adding a quick technical summary here so Sarah's team can review before the sync.

Planned retrieval/test knobs:
- Chunking: 1,000 token chunks with 200 token overlap (clinical context benefits from larger chunks for continuity).
- Embedding model: redwood-embed-3 (512-d) for initial pass; fallback to text-embedding-3-small if memory/throughput limits appear.
- Vector store: run locally on FAISS for bench; production options: Weaviate (managed) or RedisVector depending on your infra.
- Reranker options: 
  * CE-large (cross-encoder) — expected grounding-precision +12–18 pts vs bi-encoder on our internal clinical sets, latency +30–40ms on a 1-request path.
  * Hybrid (bi-encoder + CE-light on top 30) — median latency reduction ~20–25ms vs full CE, small drop in precision (~4–6 pts).
  * CE-quant (8-bit quantized cross-encoder) — cost-friendly, tails slightly worse but often acceptable for priority-2 queries.

Bench outputs we'll provide: recall@10, grounding-precision@1/3/5, avg latency (p50/p95), cost-per-1000-requests estimate, sample hallucination flags with linked doc ids.

Known risks / notes:
- If your KB contains many near-duplicate policy variants, recall can drop; we'll include dedup and canonicalization steps in preprocessing.
- Streaming UI: cross-encoder re-rank increases end-to-end response time; hybrid is often a good trade for interactive flows.

I'll post the config to the shared Drive folder and send an invite for Wed 10:00 PT.

- Dev
Engineering, Redwood Inference
